# The Broken US Healthcare System is Failing Millions of Americans with Warris Bokhari

First listed: 2026-01-12 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: The Broken US Healthcare System is Failing Millions of Americans with Warris Bokhari](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4F74GEYvtwA) - 2026-01-12
- [Substack: The Broken US Healthcare System is Failing Millions of Americans with Warris Bokhari | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 41](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-broken-us-healthcare-system-is-509) - 2026-01-12

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman and Warris Bokhari examine denial incentives, insurer ownership of care delivery, Medicare risk coding, Medicaid selection and ACA affordability. The strongest reasoning distinguishes coverage from affordability, identifies float and duration mismatches, and recognizes that a breakup cannot repair underwriting by itself. Several broad conclusions rely on selected cases or mismatched statistics: physician reimbursement becomes a pharmacy comparison, asset depletion becomes bankruptcy, and review expenses become medical spending. Claimable’s success and disruption claims remain founder assertions. No sector stock-return recommendation is inferred.

Material sector economics and policy mechanisms are retained separately from supporting factual errors. Verified definitions support some reasoning, but neither selected patient harm nor poor stock performance proves a universal deliberate-denial business model. Guest-only allegations are not attributed to Eisman.

- [Claims denials and appeals in ACA marketplace plans in 2023](https://www.kff.org/private-insurance/claims-denials-and-appeals-in-aca-marketplace-plans-in-2023/) (2025-01-27): Author analysis of CMS marketplace disclosures, not all commercial insurance. Updated page reports about 20% in-network denials; fewer than 1% appealed and 56% upheld. Initial denials later resubmitted and paid are excluded, but new claims can still secure payment. Claim counts are not unique people.

<a id="4F74GEYvtwA-c009"></a>
### 009. Medical loss ratios measure care costs relative to premiums and exclude ordinary operating expenses, so a high ratio leaves little room for profit.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 18:40-19:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4F74GEYvtwA&t=1120s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

CMS separates patient-care spending from administration and profit; regulatory adjustments and quality-improvement items mean the spoken ratio is simplified.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated mlr expense definition proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [Medicare Advantage Medical Loss Ratio](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/medical-loss-ratio) (2026-11-10): MA and Part D contract-level MLR must be at least 85%; violations can require remittances to CMS, enrollment restrictions and termination. MLR is a regulatory patient-care measure, not simply GAAP gross or net profit; it is not a universal 15% net-margin cap.

### 062. Tripling appeals from about 1% to 3% would make medical loss ratios explode because insurers must spend more on review.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:13:47-1:14:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4F74GEYvtwA&t=4427s) | Stance: endorsed | Horizon: not stated

Review expense can pressure profitability, but ordinary claims administration is not automatically medical spending in the regulatory ratio. Additional approved care could increase the numerator, and its size must be estimated separately.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated appeal cost mlr inference proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [Medicare Advantage Medical Loss Ratio](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/medical-loss-ratio) (2026-11-10): MA and Part D contract-level MLR must be at least 85%; violations can require remittances to CMS, enrollment restrictions and termination. MLR is a regulatory patient-care measure, not simply GAAP gross or net profit; it is not a universal 15% net-margin cap.

## Framework and tools

- Follow the money across insurance, providers and pharmacies rather than looking only at insurance margins.
- Separate patient access, approval, payment and ultimate affordability.
- Probe incentives with simplified arithmetic, but avoid letting illustrative margins become measured profits.
- Anecdotes motivate hypotheses; population denominators and causal counterfactuals remain essential.
